pages.title: Spelling aloud and 'a / an'

head: Written
Spoken
rows: hana dot kim at mail dot com
double-u double-u double-u dot maple dot com

rules: Say each letter separately and slowly: H – A – N – A.
For double letters say double + letter: double L.
Use an before a vowel sound: an email, an hour.

pages.head: A library card
text: Hana is new in town. On Monday she goes to the library on Maple Street. She wants a library card. The librarian, Emma, asks for her name and her email address.
Hana spells her name: H-A-N-A. Her last name is Kim: K-I-M. Her email is hana dot kim at mail dot com. Emma writes everything on a form.
Then Emma gives her a blue card. "You can borrow three books for two weeks," says Emma. Hana chooses a book about animals and says, "Thank you very much!"
tf: Emma gives Hana a red card.
pages.talk: How many books do you read a month? Where do you get them?

pages.title: Alphabet: fact file
text: The English alphabet comes from the Latin alphabet, the same as Portuguese. But there are no accents in English words (café is the only common exception).
Spelling is difficult in English: 'know' starts with a silent K, 'write' has a silent W. Do not worry: we learn word by word!
Dictionaries, phone books and school lists are in alphabetical order.
